sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with hybrid elements of European Union law and Luxembourg-specific commercial statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Treaty for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of Income and Capital (1996)
Luxembourg–Netherlands Double Taxation Convention (1968, as amended)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended)
Luxembourg–Belgium Double Taxation Treaty (1970, as amended)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment protection agreements with non-EU third countries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 13 July 2018 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE); Law of 21 December 2012 on public-interest foundations, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulations of 2018 and 2020 on the RBE and operational AML/CFT requirements; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (foreign register extract) for any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the UBO's country of origin (e.g., Dutch Chamber of Commerce, Belgian Crossroads Bank for Enterprises)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the source jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority of the UBO's nationality jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a certified French, German, or English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution confirming the banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank operating under a FATF-compliant AML/CFT framework
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer; apostille not required where the bank is regulated in the requesting jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional documentation (charter, articles of association) of any parent foundation or entity in the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if originating outside Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against UN, EU, OFAC SDN, UK HMT, and Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated sanctions lists; mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) identification and verification using a commercial risk database; enhanced due diligence (EDD) required for PEPs and for persons connected to high-risk jurisdictions; for charitable endowment entities, source of funds must be traced to documented lawful philanthropic activities; all screening results and risk assessments must be retained for at least five years following the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (www.lbr.lu / rcs.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin script and must be distinguishable from all existing names registered in the RCS. The legal name may be in Luxembourgish, French, German, or English, provided it is expressible using the Latin alphabet. If a name is submitted in another script, a transliteration must be filed, and the transliterated Latin-script version becomes the operative registered name. For an SARL, the name must end with 'SARL' or the fully spelled out 'société à responsabilité limitée'. For a private charitable foundation vehicle falling within the scope of charitable endowment management, the term 'fondation' is reserved for entities constituted under the Law of 21 December 2012, and advance approval of the Luxembourg Minister of Justice may be required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant or appointed counsel must submit a written reasoned objection within five business days of the rejection notification. If the RCS upholds the refusal, a formal administrative appeal must be lodged with the Luxembourg Minister of Justice within one month of the final rejection. The appeal must demonstrate statutory distinctiveness, non-misleading character, and absence of conflict with existing corporate names or trademarks. A new or modified name may be filed concurrently without prejudice. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, a judicial appeal may be brought before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible only as a registered-mail-address arrangement; they are not sufficient for a charitable foundation or SARL engaged in endowment management, as the entity must demonstrate real commercial substance within Luxembourg, including place of effective management, local decision-making, a Luxembourg bank account, and sufficient local staff. Registered-office service providers in Luxembourg may offer address services, but ultimate physical presence and substance must be established in line with Luxembourg tax law and general anti-abuse principles.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 15% annual probability) for a passive private charitable foundation with no financial-sector license; increases to approximately 75% if the foundation solicits third-party endowments, conducts public fundraising, or undertakes regulated asset management activities, as the CSSF and Luxembourg tax authorities may conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify real commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) name availability search per proposed company name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the RCS fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of incorporation deed (authentic act) including pre-filing notarial consultations for SARL or foundation vehicle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark for SARL charters

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Central RCS registration and mandatory publication in the Official Gazette (Mémorial C)
Business permit (autorisation d'établissement) application for a non-regulated commercial or charitable activity
UBO register (RBE) filing and due-diligence documentation package including UBO piercing and supporting evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE) and designated AML/CFT service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for UBO piercing and electronic filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of up to three foreign UBO and corporate structure documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg embassy or competent foreign apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule; estimated USD 150 per document plus courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of non-French, non-German, non-English corporate or UBO documentation
External Luxembourg law firm pre-incorporation legal advice and formation support (review of foundation charter, UBO analysis, AML/CFT risk assessment, and post-registration steps)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; approximately EUR 350–600 per hour

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, especially Title IV, Articles 101 et seq. on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (S.à r.l.); Law of 16 May 2007 on the Organisation of the Luxembourg Business Registers; Law of 19 May 2020 introducing digital procedural reforms; and, for charitable foundation status, the Luxembourg law of 21 December 2001 on foundations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), L-2914 Luxembourg, acting through the notary’s authenticated electronic filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) deposited electronically with the RCS, followed by mandatory publication in the official electronic companies gazette, the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an S.à r.l. is EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,000). The full amount must be subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be placed in a blocked bank account in the name of the company in formation; the bank’s blocking certificate is delivered to the notary. In-kind contributions require a valuation report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d’entreprises agréé). The blocked funds are released only upon successful RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] S.à r.l.
The founding members unanimously resolved:
1. The subscription of [number] shares is approved; the issued capital of EUR [amount] is fully subscribed and paid up under the notarised deed.
2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg.
3. [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) with full administration powers and [sole/joint] signature authority as per the articles.
4. The manager is authorised to open bank accounts, complete RCS, tax, and beneficial-ownership filings, and pursue the charitable foundation licensing and grant-distribution procedures.
Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and notarial execution of incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary and a Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit at least EUR 12,000. Instruct the notary to draft the articles of association, verify the corporate purpose covering endowment management and grant distribution, and include the appointment of the manager. If contributions are made in kind, obtain a statutory auditor’s valuation report. Execute the deed before the notary and deliver the bank’s capital-blocking certificate to the notary.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and passports of all founding members
Bank certificate of capital blockage and payment
Statutory auditor’s valuation report for any in-kind contribution
Manager’s written consent and declaration of acceptance
Fit-and-proper evidence or no-criminal-record certificate, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary queries the source of funds, supply certified bank statements or a source-of-funds declaration. If the notary identifies legal defects, amend and re-execute the deed before RCS submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic deposit and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the notary’s authenticated e-filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically files the certified copy of the notarised deed, the articles of association, and the RCS registration form. The RCS performs formal legal review, name-conflict verification, and assignment of the RCS registration number and legal entity identifier. Await the official certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an observation or requests clarification, the notary files a corrective rider or supplemental statement. The registration date is preserved only when the RCS confirms final formal compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official companies gazette and completion of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice – official publications service; Legilux electronic platform; coordinated by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the incorporation particulars for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Verify that the published details exactly match the deed and RCS extract, including registered office, managers, share capital, and corporate purpose.
required_dossiers: Confirmation of electronic publication fees, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains a typographical discrepancy, the notary requests a rectification publication. Legal personality is effective from RCS registration, but clean publication is necessary for full third-party effectiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social security, and charitable foundation recognition registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS), and the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice for foundation recognition
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS number to register for Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax with the ACD, for VAT with the AEDT if any taxable activity exists, and with the CCSS if employees are hired. Submit a written application to the Ministry of Justice for approval as a charitable foundation or for recognition of the grant-making public-interest purpose. Maintain a segregated endowment account and prepare a grant distribution policy for review.
required_dossiers: Grant policy, endowment budget, and intended public-benefit programme
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax authority or the Ministry of Justice queries the activity, submit a clarified business questionnaire, amend the corporate purpose, or supplement the grant policy and budget data. Late responses may be cured by voluntary correction before formal refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT, beneficial-ownership register, and premises compliance completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier), Register of Beneficial Owners hosted by the LBR, and the municipal classified-establishment and environmental service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Given the bank-wire and grant-distribution payment model, adopt a written risk-based AML/CFT policy and appoint a compliance officer. File the beneficial-ownership return with the RBE. For the physical office, submit the required municipal classement declaration or permit application, obtain fire safety inspection clearance, and complete the occupational risk assessment.
required_dossiers: Municipal classement declaration or operating permit application
Occupational health and safety risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML/RBE or premises filings are queried, remedy by filing corrected beneficial-ownership declarations and notarised manager confirmations, and by securing an updated classement decision or fire safety certificate. Late filings may be regularised with administrative fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice – Foundations and Non-Profit Organisations Division, in coordination with the Administration de l’Environnement and the municipal authority for the registered premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private charitable foundation recognition or public-interest grant-making authorisation (agrément en tant que fondation d’utilité publique), together with the municipal classified-establishment operating permit if the registered office falls within the scope of the Luxembourg law on classified establishments

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l’Environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Administrative and grant-management premises: no full EIA required; a simple classement declaration or exemption is applicable under the Luxembourg law of 9 June 2022 on classified establishments, unless the project falls within Annex II of the EIA law of 15 May 2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC-emitting industrial operations, or regulated stack emissions are authorised for passive endowment management and grant-making. All sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer connection bylaws. Office waste, including paper, packaging, and electronic equipment, must be separated and recycled under Luxembourg waste-management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Corps Grand-Ducal d’Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) is required before occupancy, including emergency exits, extinguishers, and evacuation signage. The municipal building authority must issue structural load and occupancy clearance. The Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) must accept the workplace occupational risk assessment, first-aid provisions, and workstation ergonomics.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Direct Tax Administration of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, with portal access via guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu and the eCDF filing platform; indirect taxes (VAT, registration duties) are administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); company registry functions are performed by the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), with publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed and complete the single RCSL registration through the one-stop 'Guichet unique' on MyGuichet.lu, which generates the national business registration number (matricule / numéro d'identification) used as the base tax identifier across all administrations. Step 2 — The ACD automatically opens the corporate income tax file (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax file (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax file (impôt sur la fortune) upon RCSL data transfer; formal tax registration is perfected when the matricule is referenced in the first eCDF filing. Step 3 — Apply separately to the AEDT for the Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA, format LU + 8 digits) via the MyGuichet business procedure; application must be submitted before commencing taxable activity (no notarial requirement). Step 4 — Register the charitable endowment business model with the Ministry of Justice/competent ministry if recognition of public utility status is sought; obtain the AEDT 'tax exemption file' where applicable. Step 5 — Register for municipal business tax with the relevant commune, which follows the RCSL data propagation. Non-resident owners require a local registered office, a professional director (chef d'entreprise agréé for certain regulated activities), and must appoint a designated tax representative for procedural compliance; the entire onboarding normally completes within 10-15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is a statutorily opaque legal entity subject to corporate income tax (IRC) on worldwide income at the progressive rate of 15% up to EUR 175,000 and 17% above EUR 200,000, plus a solidarity surcharge of 7% on the IRC amount (18.19% top effective IRC); municipal business tax applies at approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City (combined top rate approximately 24.94%); net wealth tax applies at 0.5% with minimum tax of EUR 535 (or EUR 3,550 where financial assets exceed 90% of total assets and EUR 350,000). The SARL is tax-resident by virtue of its registered office and effective management in Luxembourg; no territorial reduction applies. A SARL operated as a private charitable foundation does not automatically enjoy exemption: full CIT/NWT exemption is available only upon judicial or ministerial recognition of non-profit public utility status, or where the entity pursues exclusively non-commercial charitable mission per section 165 LIR, in which case non-business endowment income is exempt but commercial activities remain taxable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under section 164bis LIR for groups holding at least 95% of a resident subsidiary, permitting offset of profits and losses; (2) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under articles 60-61 of the VAT law for closely linked resident entities; (3) option to waive the EUR 35,000 small-business VAT exemption and register voluntarily; (4) election for the non-profit public utility regime with resulting CIT/NWT exemption and tax-deductible donation treatment for donors; (5) election of the investment-management fund regime if the endowment vehicle is structured as a specialized investment fund (SIF) alongside the charitable purpose. Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election; legal classification is determined by the statutory form, and hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized by mandatory ATAD anti-hybrid rules (law of 23 December 2016 and subsequent amendments).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover exclusive of VAT (small-business exemption under article 57 of the VAT law); registration becomes mandatory as of the day the threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. For non-resident suppliers, a separate EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-sales threshold and the reverse-charge regime apply, but the resident SARL is not affected. Charitable grant income is disregarded for the threshold where it constitutes true donations rather than consideration for a taxable supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg operates no real-time fiscal clearance (CTC) or digital stamping system. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only in the B2G segment (invoices to Luxembourg public-sector entities must be submitted via the PEPPOL network in EN 16931 format). B2B e-invoicing is voluntary subject to recipient acceptance; a mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime is under legislative preparation (draft tax package expected to phase in from 1 January 2026, aligned with the EU ViDA framework). Taxpayers must issue structured electronic invoices under the agreed standards when used, and all invoices must be archived in a tamper-evident electronic format for 10 years in accordance with article 56 of the VAT law; the AEDT may require access to the archived data during audits, but pre-clearance or real-time approval by the authority is not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under article 74 of the VAT law if the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter holds full transport evidence. Ancillary services directly linked to exported goods (handling, transport, inspection, loading) are zero-rated under article 75. For the charitable endowment SARL (ISIC 6430), cross-border services — grant management, endowment administration, philanthropic advisory and grant-distribution services — supplied to non-EU foundations and donors are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under B2B place-of-supply rules (customer-location principle with reverse charge in the recipient's jurisdiction); these are not treated as 'export services' requiring zero-rating documentation. Domestic services supplied for a fee to Luxembourg-resident clients are taxable at standard or reduced rates (17% standard; 14%, 8%, 3% for enumerated categories). Pure grant distributions and donations received are outside the scope of VAT in the absence of a direct consideration. The 180-day benchmark reflected in this dossier corresponds to the documentary retention and evidentiary window applied by Luxembourg customs and tax authorities for export completion files; no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline exists in Luxembourg due to full capital-account liberalization, but the 180-day period is used prudentially for customs liquidation and zero-rating proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD) export declaration accepted by Luxembourg Customs with valid Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (customs office exit confirmation, ECS/ICS records, transit documents)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR/rail consignment note evidencing carriage to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice, pro forma invoice and sales contract containing delivery terms (Incoterms)
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank statement evidencing receipt of the foreign currency consideration
Insurance certificates, packing list, weight notes and any correspondence evidencing transport instructions and export intent
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess zero-rated transactions within a 5-year standard limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or deliberate misdeclaration. Where export evidence is incomplete, the 0% rate is retrospectively clawed back and the 17% standard VAT becomes due, together with default interest normally computed at 0.6% per month (7.2% annualized) on the underpaid amount. Administrative fines for invoicing and declaration irregularities reach EUR 12,500 per violation; fraudulent export claims and forged customs documentation attract criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of directors, additional customs fraud penalties under the Union Customs Code, publication of sanctions, and personal civil liability of the SARL's managers under company law. The tax authorities apply enhanced scrutiny to recurring export patterns, rapid reimbursement requests, and transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions; clawback assessments are frequently combined with net wealth tax and corporate income tax adjustments in the same audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); banking and AML/KYC supervision is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area state with full convertibility on both current account and capital account transactions. No exchange-control approval is required for inward or outward capital movements, profit repatriation, or charitable grant remittances. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantees unconditional free movement of capital within the EU; remittance and distribution routes are subject only to EU AML/CTF rules, sanctions, tax reporting, and the statutory governance of the philanthropic foundation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts and other foreign currency earnings may be freely retained in any currency. There is no conversion timeline; the only administrative obligation is statistical reporting of cross-border payments to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes, undertaken by resident banks rather than the entity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY RATING: Medium-High for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions passporting into Luxembourg; Low for offshore non-EU/EEA EMIs without a Luxembourg branch or CSSF authorization. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot act as the primary custodian of large endowment capital, cannot issue credit or treasury products, and must comply with the Luxembourg AML/CFT framework, e-money safeguarding rules, and CSSF conduct-of-business requirements. EMIs are suitable primarily for low-value grant disbursements, operational cards, and ancillary payment flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory requirement for physical presence, but Luxembourg banks generally require at least one in-person KYC interview with the foundation directors and the underlying beneficial owners before opening an institutional account. Remote onboarding is permitted only where CSSF-compliant audio-video identification and a qualified electronic signature are used; non-resident founders and directors should anticipate a physical or notarial verification step for the initial endowment deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous beneficial ownership due to the absence of shareholders and the trust-like structure of a private charitable foundation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized foundation deed, Grand-Ducal or Ministry of Justice authorization, current register of directors, Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE) UBO filing, board resolution proving management control, and a legal opinion on the foundation's corporate governance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk donations from tax havens, sanctioned jurisdictions, or opaque third-party payors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Donor KYC file, certified gift agreement, 12 months of bank statements proving source of wealth, source-of-funds declaration, tax exemption certificate, sanctions and PEP screening evidence, and correspondent-bank confirmation where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Endowment accumulation without a credible philanthropic distribution schedule.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Grant-making policy, projected disbursement schedule, board minutes approving annual distributions, audited financial statements, and the foundation's Luxembourg philanthropic status certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Grant beneficiaries domiciled in restricted, sanctioned, or higher-risk foreign jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficiary due-diligence files, grant contracts, risk assessment and mitigation memorandum, UN/EU restrictive-measures list checks, no-shell-company certification, and a traceable fund-release instruction chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound endowment contributions must use SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer to the beneficiary IBAN (LU account), with full remitter information, transaction reference, and a clear purpose indicator such as 'CHARITABLE CONTRIBUTION', 'ENDOWMENT CAPITAL INJECTION', or 'DONATION'. The remitting and beneficiary banks verify the travel-rule dataset under EU Regulation 2015/847, screen against sanctions and AML/CTF lists, and confirm the foundation's RCS registration and tax status. Large or third-party injections require a board resolution, donor provenance evidence, and, where advisable, a Luxembourg legal opinion on the charitable purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For grant distributions within the EEA, use SEPA Credit Transfer with a UETR reference. For non-EEA disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 with a structured beneficiary line and a purpose code mapped to grants or donations. Commercial letters of credit are not suited to pure philanthropic grant flows; an LC is used only if the foundation's treasury holds genuinely trade-related assets or performs collateralized transaction operations. Every outbound instruction must pass sanctions screening, beneficiary-bank due diligence, and grant-approval reconciliation before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (up to 12 months) executed with CSSF-licensed banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or illiquid emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency swaps for matched endowment asset and liability rebalancing
Short-term FX swap/rollover contracts for treasury liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and management report where applicable) approved by shareholders and filed with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS / LBR) via e-Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholders' approval, and in any event no later than seven months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed coercive fine of EUR 20 to EUR 100 per day of delay; persistent failure may lead to court-ordered strike-off of the SARL from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the fiscal year for calendar-year taxpayers; extended electronic filing deadlines may be granted under current administrative practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of 10% of the net tax due plus late-interest at the statutory monthly rate of 0.8%; repeated failure permits ex officio assessment and enforced recovery.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return in respect of Luxembourg-situs assets and worldwide net wealth where applicable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is subject to mandatory independent audit by a rÃ©viseur d'entreprises agrÃ©Ã© if it exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds at two consecutive balance sheet dates: total assets greater than EUR 4,400,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,800,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for entities licensed by the CSSF, public-interest entities, and companies whose shares or debt instruments are listed on a regulated market.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 15 December 2010 on commercial companies, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS is permitted or required for certain consolidated financial statements and for listed entities under the specific legal provisions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation through the RBE electronic portal by 31 March each year. Any shareholding transfer resulting in a change of beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the event; the annual confirmation restates the current ownership percentages, control chain, and nature of beneficial interest.
